questions.stem: A 23-year-old man presented with dysuria, urethral itching, and clear urethral discharge. He had been treated 1 week earlier with a stat dose of azithromycin 1 g for NGU. He had not had any sex since treatment. Investigations: Gram stain showed 5 PMNs per oil immersion field NAAT for gonorrhea, chlamydia, and trichomoniasis were negative
questions.lead_in: What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Mycoplasma genitalium M. genitalium should be considered in men with persistent urethritis especially after treatment with doxycycline. Azithromycin 1 g orally as a single dose should be administered in men initially treated with doxycycline. However, azithromycin resistance is also reported in M. genitalium. C. trachomatis and N. gonorrhoeae are less likely causes based upon the negative NAAT . HSV can cause urethritis, but typically symptoms would resolve even in the absence of treatment. The absence of dermatologic findings makes contact dermatitis less likely.
questions.source: Comprehensive Review of ID · Quiz 2 Q19

questions.question: In a man who has sex with men with a sexually transmitted infection, list non-viral causes of urethritis to the species level with the treatment including dose and route according to PHAC.
questions.question_raw: AM 17. STI in MSM - list non-viral causes to species level of urethritis with the treatment including dose and route according to PHAC (4)

parts.text: List non-viral causes with treatment for Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, Mycoplasma genitalium, Mycoplasma hominis, Ureaplasma urealyticum, Trichomonas vaginalis

parts_raw.text: List non-viral causes with treatment for N. gonorrhoeae, C. trachomatis, Mycoplasma genitalium, Mycoplasma hominis, Ureaplasma urealyticum, Trichomonas vaginalis

questions.model_answer:
(1) Neisseria gonorrhoeae - ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose plus azithromycin 1 g PO single dose; do not use fluoroquinolones unless susceptibility proven; test of cure in MSM/pharyngeal disease.
(2) Chlamydia trachomatis - doxycycline 100 mg PO twice daily for 7 days, or azithromycin 1 g PO single dose.
(3) Mycoplasma genitalium - azithromycin 500 mg PO day 1 then 250 mg PO daily days 2-5; moxifloxacin 400 mg PO daily for 7 days if previously azithromycin-treated or macrolide resistance (14 days if M. genitalium-associated PID).
(4) Trichomonas vaginalis - metronidazole 2 g PO single dose, or 500 mg PO twice daily for 7 days; treat current partners.
(Ureaplasma urealyticum - doxycycline 100 mg PO twice daily for 7 days; Mycoplasma hominis is not an established cause of urethritis.)
questions.beyond_mandell: PHAC Canadian STI Guidelines provide the MSM gonorrhea regimen with test of cure and the M. genitalium and trichomoniasis dosing.

cohort_answer.text: N. gonorrhoeae - ceftriaxone 250mg IM + 1g Azithromycin. C. trachomatis - azithromycin 1g PO or doxy 100mg PO BID x7d. Trichomonas vaginalis - metronidazole 2g x1 or 500mg PO BID x7d. Mycoplasma genitalium - Azithromycin 500mg x1 then 250mg PO x2-5d (if previously treated with azithro, Moxi 400mg daily x7d; if PID, Moxi 400 x14d); NAAT is diagnostic test of choice, routine screening not recommended. Ureaplasma urealyticum - doxycycline 100mg PO BID x7 days (no PHAC guideline; Sanford: doxy or azithro 1g x1).

questions.question: Name the first-line treatment regimen for the following infections in men who have sex with men, as per the Public Health Agency of Canada.
questions.question_raw: Name the first-line treatment regimen for the following infections in men who have sex with men, as per the Public Health Agency of Canada.
questions.model_answer: a) Ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose plus azithromycin 1 g PO single dose. b) Doxycycline 100 mg PO bid for 7 days (azithromycin 1 g PO single dose alternative). c) Azithromycin 500 mg PO day 1 then 250 mg daily for 4 days (or doxycycline lead-in), with moxifloxacin 400 mg PO daily for 7–14 days for macrolide-resistant/persistent disease. d) Metronidazole 2 g PO single dose (or 500 mg PO bid for 7 days). e) Doxycycline 100 mg PO bid for 7 days (azithromycin 1 g PO alternative).
questions.beyond_mandell: Regimens are from the PHAC Canadian Guidelines on Sexually Transmitted Infections; the chapter (CDC-based) does not give Canada-specific MSM regimens.

questions.question: A 22-year-old person had a lung transplant 2 weeks ago and then presents in status epilepticus with an ammonia level of 1643 umol/L.
questions.question_raw: A 22 year old person had a lung transplant 2 weeks ago, and then presents in status epilepticus with an ammonia level of 1643 umol/L.

parts.text: Name TWO microorganisms that could cause this presentation.

parts_raw.text: Name TWO microorganisms that could cause this presentation.

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Ureaplasma urealyticum (2) Ureaplasma parvum. Disseminated Ureaplasma infection is the recognized cause of the usually fatal hyperammonemia syndrome in immunocompromised patients, particularly lung transplant recipients; both Ureaplasma species have been implicated. These infections respond to appropriate antibiotics (azithromycin plus levofloxacin initially).
questions.beyond_mandell: Mycoplasma hominis (including donor-derived) is also reported to cause post-transplant hyperammonemia (Smibert et al., CID 2017) and is an acceptable alternative organism.

questions.question: Based on PHAC guidelines, name the recommended first-line treatment (drug, dose, route, duration) for each of the following in the MSM population.
questions.question_raw: Based on PHAC guidelines, name the recommended first-line treatment for the following for the MSM community (drug, dose, route, duration).
questions.model_answer: a) Neisseria gonorrhoeae: ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose PLUS azithromycin 1 g PO single dose. b) Chlamydia trachomatis: doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x7 days (azithromycin 1 g PO single dose alternative; LGV treated x21 days). c) Trichomonas vaginalis: metronidazole 2 g PO single dose. d) Mycoplasma genitalium: azithromycin 500 mg PO day 1 then 250 mg PO daily to complete 5 days. e) Ureaplasma urealyticum: doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x7 days.
questions.beyond_mandell: Doses/durations are from PHAC Canadian Guidelines on STIs (MSM); this chapter follows CDC and does not tabulate PHAC MSM regimens.

cohort_answer.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae: Ceftriaxone 250mg IM once PLUS Azithromycin 1g PO once. Chlamydia trachomatis: Doxycycline 100mg PO bid x7 days (for LGV treat 21d). Trichomonas vaginalis: Metronidazole 2g PO once. Mycoplasma genitalium: Azithromycin 500mg PO day 1 followed by 250mg PO for total of 5d. Ureaplasma urealyticum: Doxycycline 100mg PO bid x7 days
